youtube.aciklama: Classically, longitudinal fractures of the temporal bone are more common and mostly affect the middle ear, causing a conductive loss. Transverse fractures affect the inner ear more often; sensorineural loss, vertigo and facial palsy can occur. Otic capsule violating fractures have a more severe course, and measuring air and bone conduction together shows the type of loss.
